To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proton structure function F2 and the reduced cross section d2sigma/dydxQ2 at HERA center-of-mass energy 318 GeV, measured in the kinematic region 0.05<xBj<0.35 and 5<Q2<1000GeV2, are in excellent agreement with next-to-leading order QCD predictions using parton distribution functions determined from fits to deep-inelastic scattering data from lower energies.
the structure functions F2(x,Q2) and FL(x,Q2) are well described by a QCD analysis of all available data.

the structure functions F2(x,Q2) and FL(x,Q2) are in good agreement with previous measurements, and that the Q2-dependence of the structure functions is well described by QCD fits to world data, including our data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of reduced deep-inelastic scattering cross sections at large values of the inelasticity, y.
the measurement of the proton structure function F2 and the reduced cross section dσ/dy.
the study of the proton structure in the region 10-5≤Q2<100  GeV2 and 0.002≤x≤0.6.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZEUS measurements of the proton structure functions, F2 and FL, agree well with the results from H1 and with the results of QCD fits to other measurements.
the data are in very good agreement with the Standard Model predictions.
the data show no significant evidence of new physics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the measurements of the proton structure function FL agree with the predictions from the H1 collaboration, and that our measurements are compatible with the predictions of the CTEQ6.5 and MRST2004 NLO QCD fits, and with the predictions of a leading order QCD calculation.
we have extracted the structure functions F2, F3, FL, and F2L, and we have compared our results with other measurements and with QCD fits to other data.
our measurements are in agreement with previous HERA measurements and with the predictions of the leading order (LO) and next-to-leading order (NLO) DGLAP QCD calculations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the data at the lowest energy, 225 GeV, are not consistent with the other two data sets.
the data are well described by next-to-leading-order perturbative QCD calculations based on the leading-twist structure functions.
the proton structure function F2 is not constant as x→0.
